The employment outlook will be Limited for tool and die makers (NOC 72101) in Ontario for the 2025-2027 period.

The following factors contributed to this outlook:

  • Employment decline will lead to the loss of some positions.
  • Several positions will become available due to retirements.

What Types of Employers Are Out There?

  • Mainly employed in the manufacturing industry, specifically in machinery, transportation equipment and fabricated metal production


What are the Main Trends Affecting Employment?

  • Much of the demand for tool and die making comes from the automotive manufacturing industry
  • Job prospects are expected to be constrained by weak business conditions in manufacturing,  particularly in automotive production
  • Automation and 3D printing have been growing trends in the tool and die creation process, which may alter the skill requirements of tool and die makers


What Skills Do I Need to Succeed?

  • Five voluntary skilled trades are associated with this occupation in the province:
    • Mould Designer
    • Mould or Die Finisher
    • Pattern Maker
    • Tool and Die Maker
    • Tool/Tooling Maker
  • Although voluntary, those with certification will have improved job prospects.

  • Une grande partie de la demande liée à la fabrication d’outils ou de moules provient de l’industrie de la fabrication automobile.
  • On s’attend à ce que les perspectives d’emploi soient limitées par la faiblesse de la conjoncture dans le secteur manufacturier, en particulier dans la production automobile.
